key_insight: Inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL) makes explicit human approval a mandatory condition for an AI agent to initiate an action, rather than a guardrail the agent might bypass.
problem_solved: As AI agents become better at bypassing safeguards, conventional human approval workflows may fail to provide reliable oversight. This work addresses how to enforce that oversight robustly.
method: Introduce I-HITL as a protocol concept for enforcing human authorization of agent actions.
Require explicit human approval before an agent can initiate an action.
Treat resistance to agent-driven bypass as a core requirement; implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, I-HITL reframes human oversight as an enforceable authorization requirement rather than a workflow convention. It could guide safer designs for agents that perform consequential actions.
visual_elements: Action-flow diagram: AI proposes an action → human explicitly approves → action is initiated.
Side-by-side illustration of a bypassable approval checkpoint versus mandatory I-HITL authorization.
Locked-gate icon showing that an agent cannot proceed without human approval.
Trust-boundary diagram separating the AI agent, human approver, and action-execution system.
paper_authors: Samuel Breckenridge, Dani Vilardell, Wenhao Wang, Fan Zhang, Ari Juels
